land.text: the East Javanese remnant of Mataram, whose capital Wwatan was destroyed in 1006; Airlangga 'rallied support from officials and regents that were loyal to the former Isyana dynasty'

predecessors.note: The Mataram dossier (se-02-a) dates Mataram's fall to 1016; the Kahuripan page dates the new kingdom to 1019.

land.text: the western half: 'Airlangga divided Kahuripan into two kingdoms which were inherited by his two sons; Janggala and Kediri'

successors.note: The page does not say which son took which half.

land.text: the north-eastern half, read from Cliopatria's 1046 shapes

capitals.name: Watan Mas (Wwatan)
capitals.note: The page names Watan Mas only as the capital before 1037 ('In 1037 the capital was moved from Watan Mas to Kahuripan') and gives no location or founding year; the dot is placed at Madiun, the western limit of the realm named by the page, as a placeholder.

capitals.name: Kahuripan
capitals.note: 'Kahuripan, at the Brantas River estuary near modern Surabaya and Pasuruan' (infobox); the dot is the midpoint of the two cities.

rulers.name: Airlangga
rulers.note: Kahuripan page infobox gives the reign as 1019-1045; the Airlangga page's infobox says 'Reign: ? - 1042' but its text has him abdicate in 1045. He died in 1049.

correction.text: the Kingdom of Kahuripan 'stretched from Pasuruan in the east to Madiun in the west'; Kediri is added only to join the two ends along the Brantas valley

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Kahuripan shape begins in 1028 but the page founds the kingdom in 1019 on a smaller East Javanese core. The 1028 growth is carried by the ledger. The page gives no infobox area, so there is nothing to compare with Cliopatria's 80,771 km2.

80,771 km2: on the grid it covers 170 of East Java's 197 cells, 102 of Central Java's 143, all of Yogyakarta and 22 of Bali's 24, which matches the page's 'Later, he extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali'. The page does not date that growth, so the year 1028 is Cliopatria's (ledger events at confidence 1). No infobox area on the page.

Identical to the 1028 shape; nothing on the page changes the extent between 1040 and the partition of 1045. The page's one dated change in these years is the 1037 move of the capital (no territorial effect).

region.text: the Kingdom of Kahuripan 'stretched from Pasuruan in the east to Madiun in the west'; Kediri is added only to join the two ends along the Brantas valley

ledger.note: 1019: Airlangga founds the Kingdom of Kahuripan in East Java. 'In 1019, after several years in self-imposed exile in Vanagiri hermitage, Airlangga rallied support from officials and regents that were loyal to the former Isyana dynasty... The new kingdom was called the Kingdom of Kahuripan, and stretched from Pasuruan in the east to Madiun in the west.' Cliopatria begins the polity in 1028.

region.text: the rest of Cliopatria's 1028 shape beyond the Pasuruan-Madiun core, chiefly Central Java: 'Later, he extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali'

ledger.note: c. 1028: Kahuripan grows beyond its core into Central Java. 'Later, he extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali.' The page gives no year; 1028 is Cliopatria's. Mataram, whose land this was, had fallen in 1006/1016, so no state is named as the loser.

region.text: Bali: 'Later, he extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali'

ledger.note: c. 1028: Bali is brought under Kahuripan. The page's wording is 'extended his kingdom to ... Bali' and gives no year (Cliopatria's 1028). The Airlangga page says he was 'born 1002 in Bali'; neither page says whether Bali was held directly or as an ally or vassal.

1037: Airlangga moves the capital from Watan Mas to Kahuripan. 'In 1037 the capital was moved from Watan Mas to Kahuripan.' The page also notes the trade ports Hujung Galuh (Surabaya) and Kambang Putih (Tuban).

region.text: the western half, read from Cliopatria's 1046 shape

ledger.note: 1045: Airlangga divides his kingdom and abdicates. 'In 1045, Airlangga divided Kahuripan into two kingdoms which were inherited by his two sons; Janggala and Kediri.' The page does not draw the line; the legend of Mpu Bharada pouring water to make a boundary river is told as legend. The Kediri Kingdom article (see the kediri-kingdom dossier) says 1042.

region.text: the north-eastern half, read from Cliopatria's 1046 shape

ledger.note: 1045: the second kingdom of the partition, Janggala. Same sentence as the Kediri split; the page names the two kingdoms but not their boundary.

region.text: Bali, which neither successor's Cliopatria shape includes

ledger.note: 1045: Bali drops out with the partition. The page is silent: it says only 'Later, he extended his kingdom to Central Java and Bali' and names Janggala and Kediri as the heirs; Cliopatria's 1046 shapes of both successors leave Bali out (22 cells).

1045: Kahuripan ends in the partition into Janggala and Kediri. Infobox: 'Airlangga divided his kingdom into Janggala and Panjalu (Kediri): 1045.' Airlangga died in 1049: 'After the death of Airlangga, a civil war broke out between Janggala and Panjalu that continued until 1052.'

wars.name: Wurawari rebellion against Mataram
wars.outcome: The Mataram capital Wwatan was destroyed and Airlangga went into exile; in 1019 he rallied the loyal officials and founded Kahuripan.
wars.note: 'In 1006, a rebellion incited by a vassal king Wurawari from Lwaram destroyed the capital of Wwatan.' The Airlangga page calls the destroyed capital Watugaluh and the Mataram dossier dates the fall to 1016. It fell before Kahuripan existed and moved no Kahuripan border; the page also says he 'made peace with Srivijaya' without a date.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the extent is only 'from Pasuruan in the east to Madiun in the west' and, undated, Central Java and Bali.

sources.title: Kahuripan
sources.note: Identity, founding in 1019, extent, capital move of 1037, partition of 1045. The infobox gives no area.

sources.title: Airlangga
sources.note: Cross-check: reign, 1006 destruction of the capital, abdication in 1045, death in 1049. Thin on territory; no area.

notes: Page budget 1-2 pages: Kahuripan and Airlangga. Disagreements: the Kediri Kingdom article (cited in the kediri-kingdom dossier) dates the partition to 1042, the Kahuripan page, the Airlangga text and the Janggala infobox to 1045; 1045 is used (Cliopatria's successors begin 1046). The Airlangga infobox reign '? - 1042' contradicts its own text (abdication 1045). The destroyed capital is Wwatan on the Kahuripan page and Watugaluh on the Airlangga page. Not settled: where Watan Mas was (the capital dot is a placeholder at Madiun); when Central Java and Bali were added (Cliopatria's 1028 is not on the page); whether Bali was held directly or as an ally/vassal (the Bali Kingdom page, read for the Kediri and Singhasari dossiers, says 'either Bali had allied with East Java, or Bali was Java's vassal'); whether the Srivijaya peace has a date. Predecessor: the Mataram dossier (se-02-a) ends Mataram in 1016, three years before this dossier's 1019 start. No new gazetteer names needed.
